correctness.rationale: For r,m>=2,a>=1, d=r+ma, transverse nontrivial cyclic ages are rj/a (a>1), giving ambient canonical iff a<=r and terminal iff a<r, with a=1 smooth. Fletcher Theorem 1.5.1 tests every nonempty coordinate subset: a unit-containing subset supports degree-d pure powers; for heavy-only subsets a|r supplies supported monomials; otherwise the only available outside Jacobian monomials require a|(r-1) and distinct unit coordinates. The full m-heavy subset imposes r>=m. Since gcd(r,r-1)=1, the canonical and terminal counts equal tau(r)+1_(r>=m)(tau(r-1)-1) and that minus one, respectively. Independently implemented the general subset/semigroup test from inspected criterion and verified all 128 triples r,m=2..5,a=1..8; finite replay is regression only.

originality.rationale: FAIL on the full final claim as an independent new theorem: Fletcher 1989 Theorem 1.5.1 is an iff quasismoothness classification for arbitrary weighted hypersurface weights and degree, including exactly these 1^r,a^m weights, all r,m,a and d=r+ma. The two divisibility branches and rank obstruction result immediately by substituting heavy-only coordinate subsets and counting outside unit variables; tau-count identities then mechanically count permitted divisors. Thus the proposed classification is an elementary corollary/specialization already implied by an older strictly broader iff theorem, even though the exact closed expression is not printed verbatim there. The independent subset replay verifies this implication, not a new result. No keyword match or inaccessible source is used to manufacture O failure.
